clue.text: Old dandy seen in a carriage just after joining motorway

indicators.note: the carriage pieces join the motorway by being set between its two letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI
a car is a carriage, as in a railway car
on can mean immediately following, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A fop of old is spotted riding in a coach as it comes onto the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' puts ACARON inside MI, the M1 motorway written with an I for the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: In the 18th century a fashionable fop who aped Continental styles was called by this name, as in Yankee Doodle.

clue.text: Maid causing a considerable upset

parts.note: considerable means big, large
an upset, as in a stomach upset, is an ail or ailment

explanation.surface: A servant's behaviour causes a lot of trouble in the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is a noun here, a minor illness, not an emotional state.
explanation.definitionFit: From a waiting-woman in Beaumont and Fletcher, the name became a generic word for a lady's maid.

clue.text: Hate to be a man in endless turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion, so these letters are thrown into disorder
without its end, the word in loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Hating to be a man always in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts IN to I; with TOBEAMAN that makes nine letters, which 'turmoil' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest, a stronger synonym for hate.

clue.text: Equipment not acceptable if climbing to top of tower

parts.note: out means not acceptable, as in 'that idea is out'

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the word if goes backwards
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Gear that isn't up to standard if you're scaling a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns IF into FI in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of kit or gear for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Climb supposedly having little support in Simla?

definitions.text: Climb supposedly having little support in Simla?

parts.words: Climb supposedly having little support in Simla?
parts.note: a legendary feat in which a performer is said to climb a length of cord standing upright with nothing holding it, in British India

explanation.surface: A climb in an Indian hill station with very little to hold on to.
explanation.walkthrough: Simla (Shimla) was the summer capital of British India; the legendary trick has a boy climb a rope that stands unsupported in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous conjuring illusion is a climb up a cord with supposedly no support, set in India.

clue.text: The tradition of business patronage

explanation.surface: Old practice in trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a habit or practice; it also means the regular trade a shop gets from its customers.

clue.text: Big business see girl is on the way up

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A major firm sees a young woman rising through the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns LASS into SSAL; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means huge or enormous, a stronger synonym for big.

clue.text: Percussive instrument a doctor used during a spell of duty

indicators.note: these pieces are placed within the spell of duty

parts.note: a tour is a spell of duty, as in a tour of duty
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A medic plays a drum during a shift.
explanation.walkthrough: A tambour is also embroidery frame, but here the drum; 'used during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambour is a drum, especially a small one like a tambourine.

clue.text: Caged exhibition of game set out around northern lake

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the northern abbreviation
set out means arranged afresh, so these letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A show of captive animals arranged round a lake in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges GAME to MEAG; 'around' puts it round N to make MENAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept in cages for display.

clue.text: Gear for soldier sent back to intervene in riot

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a riot or disorderly crowd

indicators.note: sent back means the word is turned round

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Kit for a soldier who is ordered back to break up a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUT is an old word for a riotous mob; 'sent back' reverses the soldier and 'to intervene in' places him inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig-out is an outfit of clothes, a colloquial word for gear.

clue.text: West Yorkshire fellow consuming prodigious meals

annotationWithheld.why: West Yorkshire fellow consuming prodigious meals (8): DALESMAN takes MEALS rearranged inside D-A-N, but no clue word cleanly supplies DAN once 'West Yorkshire fellow' is the definition, so a word would do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: West Yorkshire fellow consuming prodigious meals

clue.text: Scholar introducing glassy material in old church

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar
silica is the mineral glass is made from

explanation.surface: An academic brings glass into an ancient church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is an early Christian church built on the plan of a Roman hall.

clue.text: A redhead lay about in an oriental garment

indicators.note: the song goes round the other letters

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad
the head, or first letter, of the word red is R

explanation.surface: A red-haired woman lay around in eastern clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay' is not the verb but a noun, a ballad; 'about' puts AR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a wrapped skirt worn in Malaysia and Indonesia.

clue.text: Last of sheep allowed out of a fold

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
out of here means outside, so the permitted word goes around the a

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: The final sheep is let out of the pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' is a pen for sheep in the surface but a crease in cloth in the answer; 'out of' puts LET round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed into fabric.

clue.text: Like chauvinists quietly taking port in an upper room

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical term for quietly

indicators.note: the attic takes the port inside it

parts.note: an attic is a room at the top of a house
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Patriots quietly drink port in the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; 'taking' is the container signal, with the port held inside the upper room.
explanation.definitionFit: Chauvinism originally meant excessive love of one's country, after the French soldier Chauvin.

clue.text: One who greatly values his post as finance officer

definitions.text: One who greatly values his post as finance officer

parts.words: One who greatly values his post as finance officer
parts.note: someone who prizes or cherishes something, and also the holder of the office that looks after a club's money

explanation.surface: An official who cherishes his job looking after the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure is to value highly, and the officer in charge of funds bears the same title.

clue.text: Plain girl sailors embrace same man

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: the outer pieces close around the sailors

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same
Ed is a man's name
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A homely girl whom sailors hug is the same man.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same; 'embrace' has the man's and the same's letters around the sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadorned means without decoration, simple and plain.

clue.text: Increased total sounds ghastly

indicators.note: sounds signals that the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: increased is grew and a total is a sum

explanation.surface: The rising tally makes grim news.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrifying and repellent, close to ghastly.

clue.text: Great help, it turns out, when communicating in the bush

indicators.note: turns out means comes out differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It turns out to be a big help when sending messages in the outback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' rearranges GREATHELP.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush telegraph is the informal spreading of news by word of mouth in remote areas.

clue.text: Authorisation for debauchery

explanation.surface: Permission to be dissolute.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is a permit; licence also means excessive freedom, unrestrained or dissolute behaviour.

clue.text: Comedy produced by a churchgoer in Birkenhead

indicators.note: the churchgoer sits inside the Birkenhead letters

parts.note: F. E. Smith was the first Earl of Birkenhead, a British statesman
RC, Roman Catholic, is a churchgoer

explanation.surface: Something funny done by a worshipper in a Merseyside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Birkenhead looks like the town across the Mersey from Liverpool; here it is F. E. Smith, Lord Birkenhead, giving FE.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is a comic play built on absurd situations.

clue.text: Former Ukrainian cavalryman produces the commander's wine

parts.note: CO is the commanding officer, so CO'S is his
sack is an old white wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A horseman supplies his officer's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is the sherry-like wine Falstaff loved.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were horsemen of the steppes, famous as light cavalry for the Tsars.

clue.text: Painting a student has left in the open air

indicators.note: has left means these letters go away from the phrase

parts.note: al fresco means outdoors
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student paints outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has left' takes A and L away from ALFRESCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a picture painted on wet plaster, typically on a wall.

clue.text: Spur is visible, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: something visible is in sight

explanation.surface: The goad is in view, people report.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or stir up, as a spur urges a horse.

clue.text: Duck is swallowed by wild otter or chelonian reptile

indicators.note: the duck goes inside the scrambled letters
wild means out of control, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: A duck gets eaten by a wild otter or some reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles ISOTTER and 'swallowed by' puts O inside; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelonians are the order of turtles and their land-dwelling kin.

clue.text: Indian cooking, or toad in batter?

indicators.note: to batter is to beat out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is it Indian cuisine, or toad-in-the-hole?
explanation.walkthrough: Toad in the hole is a British dish of sausages baked in batter; 'batter' is the anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori is a style of Indian cookery using a clay oven.

clue.text: Cold refreshment for the Sabbath, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: for Christians the Sabbath is the first day of the week

explanation.surface: An ice-cream treat for the day of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundae is an ice-cream dessert with toppings.

clue.text: Bill of exchange that's recognised in Rome and Paris

parts.words: that's recognised in Rome and Paris
parts.note: the word for that in Italian is che

parts.words: that's recognised in Rome and Paris
parts.note: the word for that in French is que

explanation.surface: A banknote accepted in both Italy and France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian and French words for 'that' are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money, a kind of bill of exchange.

clue.text: Source of riches found by king on leaving capital with president

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

indicators.note: leaving means these letters depart from the capital

parts.note: London is the British capital
Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A king finds wealth when he quits the capital with the president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes ON from LONDON to give LOND.
explanation.definitionFit: The Klondike gold rush of the 1890s made the Yukon region a byword for sudden wealth.
